monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp increase in intensity and efficiency compared to last month, with fewer but harder runs — pace improved by 20 sec/km and aerobic TE rose significantly, though volume dropped substantially.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite only one run this month, the runner achieved their best-ever pace (531 sec/km) and highest aerobic training effect (3.5) — indicating exceptional effort and efficiency for that session.

goal_tracker.message: You need 36.0 more km across 9 additional sessions to match last month’s volume — averaging 4.0 km per session over the remaining 30 days.

insights.title: Efficiency dip at higher intensities
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.42 m/sec/bpm in May (lower HR, lower intensity) to 12.81 in June’s single high-HR run — suggesting diminishing return on mechanical output per heartbeat as effort crosses into Zone 3–4; consistent with the 26% time spent in Z3 and 22% in Z4 this month.

insights.title: Shift from aerobic base to threshold emphasis
insights.body: Zone 1+2 time dropped from 79% (36% Z1 + 43% Z2) in May to just 46% (14% Z1 + 32% Z2) this month, while Z3–Z4 increased from 22% to 48% — signaling a rapid, possibly unbalanced shift away from foundational aerobic development.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff emerging
insights.body: Cadence increased from 146 to 154 spm this month, while stride length remained stable (~72 cm) — vertical oscillation rose from 7.5–7.8 cm (May) to 7.9–8.3 cm (recent runs), suggesting increased bounce without meaningful stride extension, potentially reducing efficiency at faster paces.

insights.title: Limited recovery data, but low session frequency raises concern
insights.body: Only 1 run in June so far — combined with last month’s 10 runs and recent 5-run cluster in 12 days (May 20–30), suggests possible fatigue accumulation or under-recovery; no HRV or sleep metrics provided, but the jump in avg HR (+11 bpm) and VO2 max stagnation at 37.0 hint at incomplete recovery.

recommendations.action: Do a 5.5 km Zone 2 run (HR 128–135 bpm) at 550–560 sec/km pace with cadence ≥148 spm and vertical oscillation ≤7.6 cm — use your May 20 run (132 bpm, 582 sec/km, 7.5 cm VO) as pacing/effort reference.
recommendations.reason: Rebuilds aerobic base, lowers average HR, and improves efficiency — countering the Z3/Z4 dominance and efficiency drop seen this month.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 km progressive run: start at 570 sec/km (Z2), increase to 540 sec/km (upper Z3) by km 2, finish at 520 sec/km (lower Z4) for final 0.5 km — monitor HR to ensure it peaks ≤152 bpm.
recommendations.reason: Improves lactate buffering and pace adaptability while staying within safe HR limits — bridges the gap between May’s easy efforts and June’s aggressive single run.

recommendations.action: Add a 15-min post-run mobility routine focused on hip flexor release and calf elasticity after every run — especially following any session where ground contact time exceeds 315 ms (e.g., May 30: 320 ms).
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time increased from 308–316 ms in May to 320 ms on May 30 — longer contact often correlates with stiffness or fatigue; mobility helps maintain stride fluidity and reduce oscillation.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish sustainable Zone 2 endurance as the physiological foundation, recalibrate effort perception, and restore mechanical efficiency before progressing further into threshold work.
suggested_sessions: 4 km conversational pace with cadence focus (148–152 spm)
